<security_assessment>
The PKGBUILD file for the CachyOS kernel package appears to be a standard, well-structured AUR package. It follows normal packaging practices for building a custom kernel. The file contains legitimate references to the project's own GitHub repository for patches and source code, along with official NVIDIA download URLs for GPU modules. There are no signs of malicious code, backdoors, data exfiltration, or suspicious network activity. The build process uses standard AUR workflows including patch application, configuration management, and module installation. The package is designed to build a custom kernel with various optional features (RT scheduler, ZFS, NVIDIA modules, etc.) but all operations are within the scope of the application's stated purpose.

<decision>SAFE</decision>

<details>
The PKGBUILD is a standard AUR package build script for the CachyOS kernel. It follows established packaging conventions:

- Uses the project's own GitHub repository (`cachyos/linux`) for source code
- Applies patches from the project's patch repository (`cachyos/kernel-patches`)
- Builds kernel modules (NVIDIA open/580xx, ZFS, RT scheduler, r8125)
- Includes proper signing and configuration steps for Easy Anti-Cheat Linux v2
- Uses standard AUR build variables and options
- All network references point to legitimate sources (GitHub, NVIDIA official downloads)

There are no indicators of supply chain attacks, malicious code injection, or unauthorized system modifications. The file contains only expected operations for building a custom kernel - compiling, applying patches, configuring kernel parameters, and installing modules. No dangerous commands (eval, base64, curl, wget, etc.) are present in unexpected contexts, and no credentials or sensitive data are being accessed or transmitted.

The package is designed to be a "CachyOS Default Scheduler (EEVDF)" kernel with EAC (Easy Anti-Cheat) integration, which is a legitimate security feature for gaming systems. All operations are confined to the package's own scope and do not modify unrelated system files outside the kernel build process.
</details>
